# Flashcards — Topic 4: Muscular Tissue Architecture
**Total Flashcards:** 12

---

### 🎴 FC_T4_01: Skeletal Muscle Characteristics
**Category:** `Skeletal Muscle`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** Voluntary, cross-striated, multinucleated syncytial muscle fibers under somatic motor neural control.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Skeletal Muscle Characteristics" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>


---

### 🎴 FC_T4_02: Smooth Muscle Characteristics
**Category:** `Smooth Muscle`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** Involuntary, non-striated, uninucleated spindle-shaped (fusiform) cells lining visceral organs under autonomic control.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Smooth Muscle Characteristics" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>


---

### 🎴 FC_T4_03: Cardiac Muscle Characteristics
**Category:** `Cardiac Muscle`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** Involuntary, cross-striated, single-nucleated branched cardiocytes joined by specialized intercalated discs.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Cardiac Muscle Characteristics" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>


---

### 🎴 FC_T4_04: Sarcomere Definition
**Category:** `Muscle Microstructure`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** Functional contractile unit of myofibrils bounded between two adjacent Z-lines.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Sarcomere Definition" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>


---

### 🎴 FC_T4_05: Anisotropic A-Band
**Category:** `Muscle Microstructure`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** Dark central sarcomere band formed by thick myosin filaments; length remains constant during contraction.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Anisotropic A-Band" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>


---

### 🎴 FC_T4_06: Isotropic I-Band
**Category:** `Muscle Microstructure`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** Light sarcomere band containing thin actin filaments; shortens during muscle contraction.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Isotropic I-Band" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>


---

### 🎴 FC_T4_07: Role of Sarcoplasmic Reticulum & Ca2+
**Category:** `Sliding Filament Theory`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** Stores Ca2+; nerve depolarization triggers Ca2+ release to bind Troponin C, moving Tropomyosin away from actin active sites.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Role of Sarcoplasmic Reticulum & Ca2+" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>


---

### 🎴 FC_T4_08: Red Muscle Fibers (Slow-Twitch)
**Category:** `Fiber Types`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** High myoglobin and mitochondria content; rich capillary supply; slow contraction speed; high fatigue resistance.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Red Muscle Fibers (Slow-Twitch)" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>


---

### 🎴 FC_T4_09: White Muscle Fibers (Fast-Twitch)
**Category:** `Fiber Types`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** Low myoglobin; high sarcoplasmic reticulum; relies on anaerobic glycolysis; fast contraction with rapid fatigue.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="White Muscle Fibers (Fast-Twitch)" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>


---

### 🎴 FC_T4_10: Muscle Connective Tissue Sheaths
**Category:** `Muscle Anatomy`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** Endomysium (encloses single fiber), Perimysium (encloses fascicle bundle), Epimysium (encloses whole muscle belly).


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Muscle Connective Tissue Sheaths" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>


---

### 🎴 FC_T4_11: Intercalated Discs
**Category:** `Cardiac Muscle`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** Junctional structures in cardiac muscle containing Fascia Adherens, Desmosomes, and Gap Junctions for electrical syncytium.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Intercalated Discs" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>


---

### 🎴 FC_T4_12: Single-Unit vs Multi-Unit Smooth Muscle
**Category:** `Smooth Muscle`

> **💡 Answer / Definition:** Single-unit (visceral, gap junctions, myogenic e.g. gut); Multi-unit (neurogenic, independent units e.g. arrector pili).


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Single-Unit vs Multi-Unit Smooth Muscle" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>
